methodology: Cross-sectional combined score: each stock is z-scored within its sector on book-to-market (value) and on year-over-year 10-K/10-Q section-level text similarity (the 'Lazy Prices' text-change signal — stable filings outperform). The two z-scores are averaged; a stock is only scored when both factors are present. Ranking is purely cross-sectional; go long the highest scores. Every edge is measured as a beta-neutral long-short (top decile minus bottom decile) rebalanced every 21 trading days, net of transaction costs.
caveats: Research prototype, not investment advice. Past long-short backtest performance does not predict future returns.
The S&P 500 universe is survivorship-biased (today's members), which flatters the value edge; the small-cap/text universe is more conservative.
Both factors are slow (monthly-horizon) and update only when a firm files a new 10-K/10-Q or reports fundamentals — picks change gradually, not daily.
